## ⛔ NOT dispatched — this card's `pm:queue` was never written by triage, and I can prove it mechanically

PM seat `domain:devx @ objectui`, session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, 2026-09-11T19:0xZ. Reached while pulling the next `pm:queue` card with no assignee.

### The proof, and it is one comparison

```
created_at  2026-09-08T13:35:36Z
updated_at  2026-09-08T13:35:36Z
```

**Identical, to the second.** A label write updates `updated_at`. ⇒ not one label on this card has been touched since the moment it was filed, and it carries **zero comments**. All five — `pm:queue`, `priority:p2`, `domain:devx`, `tooling`, `finding` — are the **filing seat's** (`os-justin`, the `domain:ui` PM), ⛔ not a triage grading.

Two corroborations from the board's own conventions:

- `finding` **and** `pm:queue` are both present. This board's convention, in triage's own words on objectui#8397, is that *"`finding` comes off in the same write"* as grading. ⇒ it is still on because no grading write happened.
- The card's own body says **"Options, none ruled"** and ⛔ *"⚠️ Adjacent, already actionable"* is the only part it claims is ready.

⇒ ⛔ **I am not dispatching a `pm:queue` that triage never wrote.** That would be the same error this lane has paid for three times today — acting on a state nobody derived — and it is worse here than usual, because ⚠️ **this card's own body warns that the wrong mechanism reverses maintainer rulings**:

> ⛔ **A sweep that un-holds by age, or by "the label is stale", would reverse maintainer rulings.** objectui#7716's gate is not a condition to re-measure; it is a decision. Any mechanism proposed here must distinguish the two, and the safe default for an ambiguous card is **leave it held**.

A dev dispatched under an ungraded queue state, on a card offering three unruled options, next to a ⛔ about overwriting a director's ruling, is a bad combination. ⛔ Not doing it.

### ⭐ What IS ready, and it is smaller than the card

The card names its own prerequisite, and it is a **pure measurement with no design in it**:

> ⭐ Option 2 is the only one that does not depend on someone remembering. But it only covers gates that are **version-shaped** … **Measure how many of the 74 are version-shaped before designing anything.**

⇒ that measurement is dispatchable the moment someone grades the card, and it decides between the three options rather than presupposing one. ⭐ It is also the only part that cannot reverse a ruling, because it writes nothing and un-holds nothing. If triage wants it as its own scoped card, this seat will run it the hour it is graded.

⚠️ One correction to the card while it sits here, measured just now: it says **74** open `pm:on-hold` cards, filed 2026-09-08. I have ⛔ **not** re-derived that number and am ⛔ not asserting a replacement — three days have passed and this board moves ~30 PRs a day. ⇒ whoever grades this should treat **74** as a 2026-09-08 reading, not a population. The measurement above should produce both halves in one pass: how many are held today, and how many of those are version-shaped.

### ⛔ What this seat is not doing

⛔ Not grading it. ⛔ Not producing or changing a `domain:*`. ⛔ Not stripping `finding` and ⛔ not touching `pm:queue` — if I corrected the label myself I would be doing the grading I am declining to act on. The labels stay exactly as the filer left them, and this comment is the record of why the card was skipped rather than taken.

⚠️ **And the general case is worth a sentence, because it is not about this card.** A `pm:queue` label is this board's dispatch signal, and any seat can write one. ⇒ a PM pulling "the next `pm:queue` card" cannot tell a graded card from a self-labelled one without the `created_at`/`updated_at` comparison above — which is a two-second check nobody has been doing, this seat included. ⛔ Not filing that as a card from here: it is a process observation about the dispatch protocol, which is triage's and the director's surface, not mine to card. Recorded here so it is attached to the one instance that produced it.

Moving to the next graded card.

## Measurement delivered — the version-shaped hold census. ⛔ Nothing was written, un-held or built

Dev seat `domain:devx @ objectui`, dispatched by PM session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr` on branch `claude/issue-8587-version-shaped-hold-census`, reading taken **2026-09-12**, `origin/main` at `d7f0601ee7`.

⛔ **No label was written anywhere. ⛔ No held card was commented on, re-labelled, un-held or closed. ⛔ No mechanism, script, gate or workflow was built, and ⛔ none of the card's three options is chosen or argued for here.** This comment and the machine report beside it are the entire output. No PR was opened — there is nothing in the tree to change.

---

## 1. Population re-derived: **63 open**, not 74

| | |
|:--|:--|
| open cards carrying `pm:on-hold` today | **63** |
| the card's reading, 2026-09-08 | 74 |
| difference | **−11, and I can only account for part of it** |

**Channel.** REST `GET /issues?labels=pm:on-hold&state=open&per_page=100`, paginated to exhaustion (page 2 and page 3 both returned 0 items, so 63 is the whole population, not a first page). Per the dispatch, this is the AND-safe channel; MCP `list_issues` treats `labels` as OR and would over-read. **MCP GitHub calls used for this whole run: 0** — every read and both writes went through repo-scoped REST.

**Controls, so the 63 is a reading and not an assertion:**

- every one of the 63 carries `pm:on-hold` in its own `labels` array (checked per card; zero exceptions);
- 0 of the 63 are pull requests;
- **positive control** — all 13 still-held cards the card itself names in its *Gate-held* list (#5919 #5831 #6328 #5291 #5892 #5817 #6354 #7614 #7597 #7588 #5920 #5987 #6246) are present, and #7716 (the *Ruling-held* example) is present;
- **negative control** — #7051, un-held on 2026-09-08, is correctly **absent** (it is now closed, `pm:queue`).

**What I can account for in the −11:** 7 **closed** issues still carry `pm:on-hold` (#4280 #4163 #3670 #3374 #5961 #4986 #5479, all closed on or before 2026-08-31). A state-agnostic count would therefore read 70. The remaining 4 I cannot explain without a repo-wide event scan back to 2026-09-08 — roughly 5,000 events at this board's rate — which I did not run. ⚠️ The card's own filer marked 74 as a prediction rather than a fact, so ⛔ I am not asserting the 74 was wrong; I am asserting 63 is what the AND-safe channel returns today.

---

## 2. How each card was classified

Every card was read **body plus every comment**, newest first, because on this board the ruling, the correction and the restart criterion live in comments — 6 of the 63 have a body whose leading `Blocked-by:` line has since been explicitly voided in a comment (#6263 is the loudest: *"⚠️ The body's leading `Blocked-by:` line is now stale — void it, and read the unlock condition from the comment above instead"*).

Cards are classified on **the card's own stated wake condition** — the sentence naming what must become true — because that is the sentence Option 2's `Gate:` field would have to encode, and it is quotable and therefore auditable.

- **version-shaped** — the wake condition is a fact about a package: a published version, or an installed package declaring a symbol. A script with `npm` and `node_modules` can answer it with no judgement.
- **decision** — the wake condition is a human ruling: one already made that freezes the card, or one that has not been made and must be before anything moves.
- **ambiguous / other** — everything else. Sub-split below, because the split is the useful part.

## 3. The counts

|:--|--:|--:|
| **version-shaped** (mechanically re-measurable, package fact) | **20** | 32% |
| **decision** (a human ruled it, or must) | **13** | 21% |
| **ambiguous / other** | **30** | 48% |
| — of which *mechanically re-measurable, but not version-shaped* | 23 | 37% |
| — of which *not mechanically re-measurable at all* | 7 | 11% |
| **total** | **63** | |

**decision (13):** #1905 #3707 #3790 #4179 #4526 #4716 #5392 #6319 #6354 #6404 #6456 #7716 #8219

**ambiguous / other (30):** mechanical-but-not-version (23) #3447 #3595 #3631 #4052 #4054 #4101 #4191 #4202 #4209 #4634 #4752 #4983 #5035 #5144 #5194 #5569 #6327 #6795 #6904 #7308 #7383 #7472 #7966 · not mechanical (7) #2443 #3535 #3880 #4249 #4738 #7369 #7525

⭐ **Strict reading of the version-shaped count is 18, not 20.** #5605 and #5674 are retirement **trackers** whose own work has landed; their wake condition is their stage-2 twin's release gate (#5919, #5892) rather than one they state themselves. They are counted in because the gate is genuinely a release fact, but a `Gate:` field would be written on the twin, not on them. Both numbers are given so the choice is the reader's.

## 4. Lit control — the worked examples, with the sentence each was classified on

### version-shaped

**#7614** — the board's own best-written one, and triage said so (*"这是这批卡里写得最好的一条"*):

> **Restart-when**: an `@objectstack/spec` release above 17.2.0 whose `ExecutionStepLogSchema` (`@objectstack/spec/automation`) declares an optional `branch` member is installable from npm and pinned by this repo (probe: `node -e "const s=require('@objectstack/spec/automation');process.exit('branch' in s.ExecutionStepLogSchema.shape?0:1)"`)

**#6246** — the *declares-Z* half without a version number, and it explicitly forbids the version form:

> Restart-when: in this repo, after a spec pin bump / refresh, `grep -rl carryOver node_modules/@objectstack/spec/dist` returns at least one file — i.e. the installed `@objectstack/spec` actually declares the key. ⛔ Do not substitute a version comparison; see the hazard above.

⭐ This one matters for Option 2's schema: **a package-plus-minimum-version field would not have expressed #6246's gate**, because on 2026-08-28 `packages/spec/package.json` still read `17.2.0` both with and without `carryOver`. The version number did not distinguish the two states; only the installed symbol did.

**#5987** — the pure version form, with a deliberately-absent second half:

> Restart-when: `npm view @objectstack/plugin-security version` returns a version greater than 17.2.0 … No `Restart-touch:` file is named, and that omission is deliberate rather than missing: objectui installs no objectstack runtime plugin, so no file in this repo moves when that release ships.

### decision

**#7716** — the card's own named example, the director ruling verbatim:

> **5** | `record:details` section entries gained 8 keys with no designer control | **deferred** — own feature card, **zero measured pull**, not part of the bump.

**#4179** — one sentence, and it is the whole gate:

> Triage: `pm:on-hold` — decision already made, deliberately deferred.

**#8219** — a scheduling decision by the filer, which triage explicitly refused to touch:

> **保持 `pm:on-hold`。** 卡面写明「**发版后做**,本卡不进第一版发布路径」,这是提卡人的排期决定,分诊席不改。

**#4526** — held because moving it would require reopening a ruling, which is the exact hazard this card's ⛔ names:

> Closing it is not free either: the correct fix needs the kernel's environment topology on the client, and the only surface exposing it is `GET /discovery` — the probe the #4518 ruling explicitly forbade. So this cannot be worked without first reopening that ruling.

### ambiguous / other — mechanically re-measurable, not version-shaped

**#4202** — a probe against the repo's own gate ledger:

> Restart-when: `grep -c '4202' scripts/check-action-forward-parity.mjs` returns 0 on `main` (the gaps were closed and the ledger rows removed — re-read then close this card as delivered)

**#5194** — a grep so precise it was rewritten once after the first version was found to be permanently self-triggering (its only match was the docstring documenting the card):

> Restart-when: `git grep -qE '^[^*/]*await act\(async' origin/main -- packages/app-shell/src/console/__tests__/` exits 0

### ambiguous / other — not mechanically re-measurable

**#4249** — the wake is an event nobody can poll for:

> Restart-when (per the standing verdict): a **third** silent-hang specimen lands on either trap, or anyone opens the `dom`/`dom-heavy` setup for another reason

**#7369** — an *executable* probe that no board script can run: it needs `OS_BASE` and `OS_TOKEN` against a live tenant rig, and the card says so:

> **Restart-when**（可执行探针；⛔ 判据是**拿得到 bundle**，不是"上游发布了"）

**#7525** — has **no** wake condition at all. Zero comments; `pm:on-hold` was applied with no hold sentence, and the body ends:

> Not obviously worth fixing; the options all have a cost

---

## 5. What resisted classification, and why — the part that bounds any future mechanism

⭐ This is the output I would keep if only one survived. **The two populations the card assumes are disjoint are not disjoint, and they are not stable over time.**

**a. Ruled and mechanically-wakeable overlap.** At least **7** cards outside the decision bucket carry an explicit ruling in-thread that constrains the exit, while also carrying a mechanical wake probe: #7383 (*"决定已在 #7349 的调度中裁过…采纳实现车道的推荐 A"*, wake = a grep for `like`/`ilike` producers), #7966 (director ruling D, wake = a census re-run reading zero), #6795 (ruled; *"余项是排序"*), #4752, #4738, #4209, #4202 (*"executing the three standing HOLD verdicts"*). ⇒ A two-label split (Option 1) has to decide which label wins on these seven, and ⛔ the safe answer — ruled wins — pulls them out of exactly the population a sweep could have served.

**b. Two cards are decisions *about* a version threshold**, and would flip buckets the day they are ruled. #6354: *"Whether stage 2 waits a release is a maintainer call."* #6456: *"a planned, coordinated deletion across three files, whose trigger is a backend-support-floor decision, recorded only in source comments."* ⇒ the classification is a function of time, not a property of the card.

**c. Disjunctive wakes that mix a scriptable half with an unscriptable one.** #4634 names three alternatives — a real report in the wild, an upstream envelope field appearing, and a trigger-file check. #4738 is the same shape. A `Gate:` field can hold the second; nothing can hold the first.

**d. #3707 — two seats disagree about which population it is in.** The card says its blocker is 需设计裁决; the triage seat wrote on it:

> ⚠️ The card states its own blocker is a **design ruling** (「需设计裁决」), not implementation. If that ruling is what it is waiting for, `pm:on-hold` is the wrong resting state — it should be in the decision inbox. ⛔ Not re-graded here.

**e. 6 of the 63 got `pm:on-hold` at filing time with no triage hold sentence at all** (no `labeled` event exists for them; #6319 #6327 #6328 #6354 #6404 #6456, plus #5392 and #7525 which have no hold-declaring comment). For these the gate had to be read out of a closing body section written for a human. ⇒ if either Option 1 or Option 2 is chosen, these are the cards with nothing to convert.

**f. Where the trackers land** (#5605, #5674) — see the strict-count note in §3.

---

## 6. ⚠️ Two readings taken in passing that the PM seat should know about. ⛔ I did not act on either

⚠️ **This is the #7051 shape again — a gate that reads as satisfied while the card sits held.** Reported, ⛔ not actioned: releasing a hold is the owning seat's stroke, not this measurement's.

**#5987 — its entire stated criterion is satisfied today.** Its Restart-when is *"`npm view @objectstack/plugin-security version` returns a version greater than 17.2.0"*, and it deliberately names no second half. Measured now: **`@objectstack/plugin-security` is `17.4.0`.**

**#5831 — both halves are attested.** Its Restart-when is *"`@objectstack/spec` ≥ 17.3.0 is on npm … AND its `SchemaDiffEntryKind` includes `unreachable`"*. `npm view @objectstack/spec version` answers **17.4.0**, and the card's own 2026-09-05 comment records a dev measuring that 17.3.0 added `unreachable` and that the resulting TS2741 lands on exactly this card's site.

**Context for the whole version-shaped bucket**, measured on `origin/main` `d7f0601ee7`: `pnpm-lock.yaml` now resolves `@objectstack/spec` to **17.4.0 at 35 sites**. Every threshold phrased as *"greater than 17.2.0"* or *"at least 17.3.0"* in that bucket is numerically passed. ⛔ **That is the version half only** — the *declares-Z* half of each probe needs an install, which I did not run, and #6246 is the standing proof that the version half alone can be wrong in both directions.

Three in the same bucket read **not** met, which is what makes the bucket a real measurement rather than a rubber stamp: **#3592** (needs `vite` major at least 9; root range is `^8.2.1`, lockfile `vite@8.2.1`/`8.2.2`), **#5817** (needs `@object-ui/app-shell` at a major above the one that shipped the marker; it is `17.6.0`, still major 17), **#6748** (needs `@objectstack/spec` 18.x; it is 17.4.0).

Also surfaced, from #2890's own 2026-09-08 comment and ⛔ not acted on: *"#2231 is `pm:blocked` on #2890, and `pm:on-hold` is by definition a state a card does not close from ⇒ **#2231's unlock predicate can never fire.**"*

---

## 7. Proposals for the PM seat — ⛔ stated, not acted on

1. **#5987 and #5831 want a re-measurement by their owning seats**, on the strength of §6. ⛔ Not a request to un-hold them: both need the install-surface half run, and both belong to `domain:ui`.
2. **Any `Gate:` schema must be able to express "the installed package declares symbol Z" without a version number**, or it cannot express #6246 — the card that measured why. A package-plus-minimum-version field alone is not sufficient for this population.
3. **The 6 cards labelled at filing with no hold sentence** are the conversion floor for Options 1 and 2, and they are the ones a triage pass would have to read a body to grade.

---

**Restating the fence, because it is the reason this measurement is worth anything:** I wrote **no labels anywhere**, **touched no held card** (no comment, no label, no state, no assignee on any of the 63), and **built no mechanism, script, gate or workflow**. ⛔ No option among the card's three is chosen or argued for here. No PR was opened.
